planning_notes: Use RTClib RTC_DS1307 initialization and a single setup-time acquisition; do not poll or repeat reports in the loop.
The SysML model gates the single report on RTC validity and retains the captured epoch. No failure message is specified; suppress the time report if initialization or acquisition fails.
Preserve SDA on A4, SCL on A5, power on 5V, and ground on GND.2. Power and ground require no model interfaces.
The supplied 2024-11-24T04:48:00 value initializes the simulated RTC only; never adjust the RTC or substitute this timestamp for an acquired reading.
Render the RTC calendar time without a timezone offset, using full English weekday names and the required YYYY/M/D (weekday) H:M:S format.
Initialize Serial at 9600 baud and complete setup within 500 ms. No serial receiver or receive framing is needed.
No business-time input is required for this startup-only acquisition and report.

configuration_resolution.original_requirement:
# RTC module

## Project Description
This is a simple Arduino project that uses RTC module to get current time.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- RTC module

## Circuit Description
The RTC module is connected to the Arduino. The VCC pin is connected to 5V, the GND pin to gnd2, the SDA pin to A4, and the SCL pin to A5.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Initialize serial communication
2. Check if the RTC module can begin
3. Read current time with RTC module
4. Print to the serial monitor in the following format: "Current time: YYYY/M/D (Day of the week) H:M:S"

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. Correct day and time is printed in the serial monitor.

## Notes for Implementation
- No actions are required in the loop function.
- Day of the week is one of the "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday".
- Use RTClib to generate RTC_DS1307 object and read the value.
- RTC module has I2C interface.

## Variants
There may be variants with GND pin.

## Test Inputs
Test init value is: "2024-11-24T04:48:00"
Given circuit (must preserve wiring):
{
    "version": 1.0,
    "author": "Blind Author",
    "description": "Get the current time using an RTC sensor",
    "config": {
        "gnd_pin": "GND.2",
        "vcc_pin": "5V"
    },
    "parts": [
        {
            "id": "arduino uno1",
            "type": "wokwi-arduino-uno",
            "top": 0,
            "left": 20
        },
        {
            "id": "ds1307 real time clock module1307",
            "type": "wokwi-ds1307",
            "top": 250,
            "left": 220,
            "attrs": {
                "initTime": "2024-11-24T04:48:00"
            }
        }
    ],
    "connections": [
        [
            "arduino uno1:GND.2",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:GND",
            "black",
            [
                "v20",
                "*",
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:5V",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:5V",
            "red",
            [
                "v0"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:A4",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:SDA",
            "green",
            [
                "v16",
                "h0",
                "*",
                "h-34"
            ]
        ],
        [
            "arduino uno1:A5",
            "ds1307 real time clock module1307:SCL",
            "orange",
            [
                "v20",
                "*",
                "h-30"
            ]
        ]
    ]
}

Operational acceptance profile operational-acceptance-v4 (additional public experimental conditions, not raw dataset text):
- Explicit original requirements and supplied circuit connections override every default below.
- Where no electrical wiring is supplied, individual LEDs are active HIGH to GND and buttons connect the named input to GND with INPUT_PULLUP; model pressed values are normalized independently of electrical level.
- When unspecified, a counter starts at zero and an LED starts OFF. An explicitly required ON state takes precedence.
- When the original gives no reaction deadline, a digital/button/serial command, PWM duty command or servo ANGLE COMMAND must update within 250ms of its input event becoming available. This does not impose physical motor travel time, shorten an explicit delay, or change a specified sensor/report period.
- When the original gives no display refresh period or response deadline, a changed input must be reflected in the display within 250ms. Explicit original display periods, delays and startup sequences override this default. This additional display bound was explicitly authorized for this experimental variant.
- Where the requirement asks to continuously stream a Boolean button/switch state over Serial but gives no repeat interval, respond to a changed state within 250ms and emit its correct state message at least once in every 500ms stable-state interval after settling. Explicit original report periods and event-only reporting rules override this default. This authorized additional continuous-state-report condition does not apply to startup-only messages, command echoes, sensor sampling or persistent display contents. A display retaining the correct visible state requires no repeated print calls unless the source explicitly requires redraws.
- Unless the original specifies a warmup or delayed startup, setup() must return within 500ms. Deadlines stated after initialization are measured from the observed setup() return, not power-on.
- An unspecified continuous DHT report must eventually emit a fresh valid reading within 3000ms of that measurement becoming available; explicit reporting periods override this bound.
